evals.prompt: Our network team is connecting our Mumbai colocation cage to AWS (`ap-south-1`) for the first time and keeps confusing **Dedicated Connection**, **Hosted Connection**, **Hosted Virtual Interface (VIF)**, and **Link Aggregation Group (LAG)**. Clarify the differences, port speed immutability, and how to pick the right model for a `10 Gbps` dual-router link.
expectations: Activates the directconnect skill

Distinguishes **Dedicated Connection** (`1G`/`10G`/`100G`/`400G` physical single-customer cross-connect with AWS LOA-CFA supporting many VIFs), **Hosted Connection** (`50 Mbps`–`25 Gbps`+ provisioned via a Direct Connect Partner supporting `1` VIF), and **Hosted VIF** (single VIF shared from a partner's connection)
Recommends a resilient dual-connection Direct Connect architecture (Dedicated Connections when colocation cross-connects fit, or Partner Hosted Connections otherwise)

evals.prompt: After our physical Direct Connect cross-connect goes `available`, compare **Private VIF**, **Public VIF**, and **Transit VIF**, explain how 802.1Q VLAN tags, BGP ASN / MD5 auth, and jumbo-frame MTU (`9001` vs `8500`) differ across them, and recommend which VIF we need to reach 12 VPCs attached to an AWS Transit Gateway.
expectations: Activates the directconnect skill

Contrasts **Private VIF** (VPC/DXGW private IPv4/IPv6), **Public VIF** (AWS public service endpoints over BGP public prefixes), and **Transit VIF** (attaches to Direct Connect Gateway to reach AWS Transit Gateways)
Recommends **Transit VIF -> Direct Connect Gateway -> Transit Gateway** for multi-VPC routing and covers BGP ASN and MD5 authentication bring-up essentials

evals.prompt: Our banking regulator just flagged that AWS Direct Connect is NOT encrypted in transit by default! Compare **MACsec (IEEE 802.1AE Layer 2)** vs **Private IP Site-to-Site VPN over a Transit VIF (Layer 3 IPsec)** across supported speeds/connections, end-to-end boundary, throughput caps, and redundancy.
expectations: Activates the directconnect skill

Confirms Direct Connect is **unencrypted by default** and compares **MACsec** (line-rate Layer-2 hop-by-hop encryption on `10 Gbps` / `100 Gbps` / `400 Gbps` **Dedicated Connections** at MACsec-capable locations, terminating at the AWS Direct Connect edge device) against **Private IP Site-to-Site VPN over a Transit VIF + DX Gateway + TGW** (Layer-3 IPsec encryption all the way to AWS TGW, works on Hosted AND Dedicated connections, ~`1.25 Gbps` per VPN tunnel scalable via ECMP across multiple tunnels)

evals.prompt: We have a single 10 Gbps Direct Connect link today and suffered a 4-hour outage during fiber maintenance, plus BGP took 90 seconds to fail over to our backup VPN! Design a **`99.99%` SLA** topology per the AWS Direct Connect Resiliency Toolkit AND tune sub-second failover convergence using **BFD** and BGP communities.
expectations: Activates the directconnect skill

Specifies AWS Direct Connect's **Maximum Resiliency (`99.99%` SLA)** topology: **4 dedicated connections across 2 distinct Direct Connect locations** (2 connections on separate AWS devices per location) vs High Resiliency (`99.9%` SLA: 2 connections across 2 locations)

Tunes fast failover via **Bidirectional Forwarding Detection (BFD)** (e.g., `300ms` interval × `3` multiplier = `< 1s` detection vs `90s` default BGP hold timer!), **BGP Local Preference communities** (`7224:7100` Low, `7224:7200` Medium, `7224:7300` High) for AWS->on-prem return traffic, and `AS_PATH` prepending / `LOCAL_PREF` for outbound traffic

evals.prompt: We started with 1 VPC connected via a **Private VIF -> Virtual Private Gateway (VGW)**, and now have 9 VPCs and need to migrate our Direct Connect setup to **Transit VIF -> Direct Connect Gateway -> Transit Gateway** without dropping live production packets! Provide the exact order-dependent cutover sequence.
expectations: Activates the directconnect skill
Warns that migrating in place / out of order drops production traffic and ensures advertised prefixes / `AllowedPrefixesToDirectConnectGateway` avoid unintended CIDR overlap

Sequences a parallel side-by-side build & cutover: provision DX Gateway + Transit VIF + BGP alongside the existing Private VIF/VGW, attach VPCs to Transit Gateway and associate DX Gateway <-> TGW, shift routing preference onto the new Transit VIF path and verify traffic cutover before deleting the old Private VIF/VGW

evals.prompt: Show how a single global **Direct Connect Gateway** lets our Mumbai and Frankfurt data centers reach Transit Gateways in `ap-south-1` and `eu-central-1` across multiple AWS accounts, AND explain the critical **`AllowedPrefixes` supernet route-leak trap** that accidentally bridges Dev VPCs to Prod VPCs!
expectations: Activates the directconnect skill

Explains the cross-account TGW association handshake (`create-transit-gateway-connect` / `create-direct-connect-gateway-association-proposal` in the TGW owner account -> `accept-direct-connect-gateway-association-proposal` in the DX Gateway owner account, max TGW limits per DXGW)

Warns against advertising a broad supernet (e.g., `10.0.0.0/8`) in `AllowedPrefixes` that overlaps Dev and Prod VPC CIDRs when on-prem routers hairpin traffic — recommending exact per-VPC prefixes, TGW blackhole routes, or separate DX Gateways

evals.prompt: Our network engineer has a 2-member `10 Gbps` Direct Connect **Link Aggregation Group (LAG)** (`minimumLinks = 2`) and is about to run `disassociate-connection-from-lag` on 1 member to move it to a new router! Stop them and explain what happens to the ENTIRE LAG when active members drop below `minimumLinks`, plus the safe procedure.
expectations: Activates the directconnect skill
Warns immediately that when operational member links drop below `minimumLinks` (`2 -> 1 < 2`), **AWS brings down the ENTIRE LAG logical interface**, causing a 100% outage!

Provides the safe order: first lower `minimumLinks` to `1` via `update-lag --lag-id <id> --minimum-links 1` (during a maintenance window, after verifying 10 Gbps single-link headroom), THEN disassociate the member

evals.prompt: Our company already has Direct Connect VIFs in `ap-south-1` (Mumbai office) and `us-east-1` (New York office) attached to the same Direct Connect Gateway, and wants Mumbai <-> New York office-to-office traffic to ride the private AWS global backbone instead of buying expensive MPLS circuits. Show how **Direct Connect SiteLink** works and its billing/security caveats.
expectations: Activates the directconnect skill

Explains enabling `SiteLink` (`--enable-site-link`) on Private or Transit VIFs attached to the same Direct Connect Gateway so on-premises branch sites exchange BGP routes directly over the AWS global backbone without hair-pinning through a Regional VPC
Covers SiteLink per-GB data transfer billing caveats, route-leak / overlapping CIDR precautions, and IPsec end-to-end vs MACsec Layer-2 encryption considerations

evals.prompt: Inspect `ap-south-1` in our live AWS account (read-only) for any existing AWS Direct Connect connections, LAGs, virtual interfaces, and Direct Connect Gateways, and summarize the mandatory monitoring, CloudTrail, and least-privilege IAM posture.
expectations: Activates the directconnect skill and inspects live `ap-south-1` Direct Connect connections, LAGs, VIFs, and Direct Connect Gateways via connected AWS MCP tools with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands

Accurately reports the live `ap-south-1` inventory (cleanly reporting 0 resources when none exist) and covers Direct Connect monitoring, CloudTrail auditing, KMS-encrypted logs, and least-privilege `arn:aws:directconnect:...` IAM scoping

evals.prompt: Query AWS documentation via connected AWS documentation tools to verify the exact AWS Direct Connect **BGP community tags** for: (1) return-traffic preference (`7224:7100`, `7224:7200`, `7224:7300`) and (2) Public VIF propagation scope (`7224:9100` local Region, `7224:9200` continent, `7224:9300` global / `NO_EXPORT`).
expectations: Activates the directconnect skill and queries connected AWS documentation MCP tools (`awsknowledge`, `aws-mcp`, or `awsiac`)

Confirms Private/Transit VIF local-preference communities (`7224:7100` Low, `7224:7200` Medium, `7224:7300` High) and Public VIF scope propagation communities (`7224:9100` local AWS Region, `7224:9200` all AWS Regions on same continent, `7224:9300` global AWS public Regions)
